new_defect_A.title: k6 0.54.0's --summary-export JSON reports every arrival-rate-executor threshold as false, regardless of the measured value -- while the CLI's own human summary shows the identical threshold passing
new_defect_A.severity: critical -- makes every k6-based assert: entry unusable for any torture.yaml, since R-CFG-6 mandates the arrival-rate executor family exclusively
reproduction: internal/run pipeline: case 8 (control, no fault) with p(95)<500 -- measured p95 29.6ms, JSON says {"ok": false}
internal/run pipeline: case 8 re-run with a deliberately generous p(95)<5000 -- measured p95 ~2-70ms across three runs, JSON still says {"ok": false} every time

Standalone, entirely outside TortureU: a hand-written k6 script using ramping-arrival-rate with a generous p(95)<5000ms threshold against a trivial always-200 Python HTTP server -- CLI prints a green checkmark, --summary-export JSON says {"p(95)<5000": false}
Standalone, constant-arrival-rate executor (not ramping) -- identical mismatch

Control: the DEFAULT executor (plain vus/iterations, a closed model) does NOT show this mismatch -- CLI and JSON agree. The bug is specific to the arrival-rate executor family k6.Compile is required to emit (R-CFG-6).
new_defect_A.consequence: internal/k6.IngestSummary and internal/run.evaluateThresholds are only permitted to read this JSON (R-VER-10 forbids parsing the human CLI text). Since the JSON's threshold field is wrong for the one executor family TortureU is allowed to generate, every real run's k6-based assertions report broken, unconditionally -- independent of whether the SUT has any defect at all. This is a 100% false-positive mechanism for the control case, and it also means a genuine defect case's 'detection' can never be distinguished from this background noise.
new_defect_A.owner: internal/k6 (IngestSummary) and/or internal/run (evaluateThresholds) -- both out of this task's edit scope. Reported, not patched.

new_defect_B.title: k6 writes console.log() output (the R-EXE-8 phase-marker mechanism) to stderr, not stdout -- but internal/run/load.go's scanMarkers only reads the process's stdout pipe
new_defect_B.severity: critical -- every phase-anchored fault (at: <phase name>, the corpus's and the spec's primary anchor mechanism; only the t=<duration> absolute escape hatch is unaffected) never fires, in any run
reproduction: Ran the exact k6 script internal/k6.Compile generated for case 1, redirecting stdout and stderr to separate files: 0 TORTUREU_PHASE_START lines on stdout, 2 on stderr (formatted as k6's own structured log lines, e.g. `level=info msg="TORTUREU_PHASE_START peak ..." source=console`).

Consequence observed directly in the real pipeline: case 1's `at: peak` fault produces status:error, "fault \"dep_slow\": load ended before phase \"peak\" started -- the fault never fired (R-EXE-19)" -- even though the phase actually started (its marker is visible in the captured stderr) -- because scheduleFaults is listening on a channel fed only from stdout, which never receives it.
Switching case 1's fault to the t=8s absolute-time escape hatch (which needs no marker) does let Run proceed past fault scheduling, confirming the marker channel is the specific point of failure.
new_defect_B.consequence: R-EXE-19 does fail the run loudly rather than silently proceeding as if the fault had applied, which is the honest behavior the codebase intends elsewhere -- but the practical effect is that no phase-anchored fault in this corpus (case 1 as designed, and every other case using `at: peak` or similar) can currently be exercised at all. Only the t= escape hatch reaches assertion evaluation, where defect A then takes over.
new_defect_B.owner: internal/run/load.go (scanMarkers reads cmd.StdoutPipe() only) and/or internal/k6 (script does not force --log-output=stdout or route console output through the stdout-based marker protocol). Out of this task's edit scope. Reported, not patched.

cases_2_to_7: not built. Both defects are structural: A means every control-like run shows a false breach regardless of threshold value, and B means every phase-anchored fault (the corpus's intended design) never fires at all. Building six more fixtures would reproduce one or both of these two already-diagnosed bugs six more times without adding information about attribution accuracy specifically.
